subject: method:direct_exact_solve_small_linear_allocation
claim: For a SMALL linear allocation MILP - two integer decision variables, one shared budget/capacity cap, at most one linear difference (effort/precedence) constraint, linear cost objective (structural cell class=milp, resource_coupling=1.0) - model it directly as one integer program and solve with a mature exact solver (CP-SAT or a HiGHS MILP) at zero MIP gap: it returns a PROVEN-OPTIMAL allocation at negligible solver runtime (~0.06 s). Decomposition, heuristics, or per-case reformulation are unnecessary. Confirmed on two DISTINCT tasks under two different family labels: (resource_allocation) optimal 10000 at (x=200,y=0); (planning) optimal 8350 at (X=167,Y=0); both matched their declared bench references. Propensity: transfer by structure (cell), not by family label.

method.name: direct_exact_solve_small_linear_allocation
steps: declare the two allocation variables as non-negative INTEGER variables (unit costs and the cap are read back from the task text)
encode the single shared capacity constraint (sum <= cap) and the linear difference constraint (coef1*X - coef2*Y >= rhs) as hard linear constraints
minimize the linear cost objective with a mature exact solver (CP-SAT, or HiGHS MIP with mip_rel_gap=mip_abs_gap=0)
report the solver status, proven optimum, and the (X, Y) allocation values
method.why: the model is a tiny, fully linear MIP, so exact branch-and-bound closes at the root; no decomposition or heuristic is warranted.
method.fallback: if the exact solver is unavailable, enumerate the (small) integer domain of one variable and take the cost-monotone boundary of the other.

conditions.note: Boundary: applies to tiny (2-decision) linear allocation instances; larger or multi-resource coupled allocations may need decomposition. The two observations carry different family labels (resource_allocation vs planning), so propagate by structural cell, not family.
